lines.text: You can see this frog's heart beating.
But what it does while it sleeps is even stranger.
Most glass frogs are just two to three centimeters long.
lines.caption: Most glass frogs are just 2–3 cm long.

lines.text: Many have see-through belly skin, so you can watch their heart and organs.
When they sleep, they pack nearly ninety percent of their red blood cells into their liver.
lines.caption: When they sleep, they pack nearly 90% of their red blood cells into their liver.

lines.text: That liver is coated in mirror-like crystals, so the blood stays hidden.
Now they're two to three times more see-through. When they wake, the blood flows back.
lines.caption: Now they're 2–3× more see-through. When they wake, the blood flows back.

lines.text: Sounds fake? It's true. Follow for more.
